evals.name: vague-ask-sharpen-and-do
evals.prompt: can you write me something to check my csv of contacts is clean before i upload it
evals.expected_output: Sharpens the ask inline (states the reading + assumptions in a line or two), then delivers a working validation script in the same turn. Does not stop to ask clarifying questions, and does not print a formal 'optimised prompt' block for approval.
assertions: Delivers a working, runnable validation script in the same turn
States its reading of the request and the assumptions it is running with
Does not stop and ask a clarifying question instead of doing the work
Does not print a formal 'optimised prompt' block for approval
Does not narrate the artifact: no walkthrough section restating flags or checks the script already self-documents
Prose outside of code is under 350 words

evals.name: big-job-sequenced-plan
evals.prompt: I want to build a full backtesting and optimisation pipeline for my cTrader bots - data ingestion, walk-forward testing, a results dashboard, and something that flags overfitting. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Returns a sequenced plan of self-contained prompts rather than starting to code. Puts the highest-uncertainty step first. Each step names its artifact, its prompt, and where/which model to run it. Offers to start step one rather than silently beginning.
assertions: Returns a sequenced plan of steps rather than beginning to write pipeline code
Each step names the concrete artifact it produces
Each step includes a self-contained prompt the user could paste into a fresh session
Each step says where to run it (fresh session vs continue) and/or which model to use
The highest-uncertainty step is placed first
Ends by offering to start step one rather than silently starting it
Connective prose is minimal: no step carries more than about three sentences of commentary outside its prompt block

evals.name: explicit-usage-worry
evals.prompt: I'm burning through my Claude Pro limit way too fast lately. I use it for trading bot code, workshop reports for work, and a react app for my wife's business. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Concrete, concise triage tied to the three named workstreams - model routing, chat vs Claude Code for repo work, session boundaries, scripting the repetitive report work. Not a generic prompt-engineering lecture.
assertions: Advice is tied to the three named workstreams, not generic prompt-engineering tips
Recommends model routing, naming at least two of Opus / Sonnet / Haiku with the work each suits
Recommends Claude Code over chat for the multi-file repo work
Recommends turning the repeated workshop-report work into a script or a reusable skill
Mentions session boundaries or context growth as a cost driver
Recommends asking for diffs/patches over full-file rewrites, or batching revisions into one message
Addresses whether this is a capacity mismatch rather than only a technique problem
Under 450 words

evals.name: already-specific-stay-quiet
evals.prompt: In my React file CharneCLient the loading spinner renders before the POPIA consent gate is checked. Move the consent check ahead of the loading state so the gate renders first. The relevant code is at the bottom of the default export.
evals.expected_output: Just does the edit. No prompt-engineering commentary, no efficiency advice, no restating of the request as an improved prompt. The guard against the skill becoming the waste it is meant to prevent.
assertions: The edit was actually made: the consent check precedes the loading check in the edited file
Contains no prompt-engineering or usage-efficiency commentary
Does not restate the user's request as an improved or 'sharpened' prompt
Applies a fix for the regression it identifies rather than stopping to ask which fix the user wants
Any caveat raised is about the code's behaviour, not about how the user phrased the request
